_about.what: Numbers and words every move shares. Edit here once and every move follows. Restart the server (or reload the page) to pick up a change.
_about.care: These affect every move at once. Change one value at a time and re-run: node scripts/catalog.js check

fields.rep: How far through a rep (0 = start position, 1 = target) the counter treats as resting, attempting and complete. rest: back below this and the rep is over. attempt: above this and a rep has started. full: reach this and the rep counts as a full one; between attempt and full it is a partial. Good: 0.15 / 0.32 / 0.85. Bad: full at 1.0 (nobody hits the target exactly, no rep would ever count) or rest above attempt. startAgain: each rep is measured from the position the person was in just before it, not from the one they were in at the start of the set — lie down a little differently on the fourth bridge and the fourth bridge is still read correctly. still: milliseconds the reading must sit still between reps before it is taken as the next rep’s start. drift: how far that start may wander from the one calibrated at the beginning, as a share of the distance from it to the target — it tracks a body that settles, without letting someone who stops half way down redefine the exercise. Good: 400 ms, 0.4. Bad: drift at 1 (a rest half way up becomes the new floor and half a rep counts as a rep) or 0 (a body that settles is read wrong for the rest of the set).
fields.still: When the body counts as having stopped, and what waits for it. move / window: how far the mid-hip may travel, as a share of the frame height, over that many milliseconds — measured over a window rather than between two frames, because at 55 frames a second a person lowering themselves onto a mat moves about 0.004 from one frame to the next and a per-frame tolerance big enough to be meaningful never fires at all. On a recorded bridge set the hip moved 0.003 over 400 ms while the person lay settled, 0.006 between reps, 0.035 through the count-in and 0.064 in the middle of a rep. hold / file: how long it must be still before the count-in starts, from the camera and from a video file — the same, because a file run through the coach is a coached set and the person in it settles at the same speed; a shorter wait for files calibrated a bridge with the person still propped up on their elbows. judge: how long before the start position is judged at all — shorter than hold, so the verdict is in before the set would begin, and nothing is named while the person is still getting there. ready / readyWait: at the end of the count-in everything the set is measured against is read, so it is read from a body that has stopped — ready is how long it must have stopped for, readyWait how long the count will hold for it before starting anyway. Good: 0.02 over 400 ms. Bad: a move so big nothing is ever moving (the old 0.012 per frame), or so small the set never starts.
fields.fault.persist: Milliseconds a fault has to be true, continuously, before it is spoken. Filters out one-frame wobbles. Good: 300–600. Bad: 0 (every jitter cues) or 3000 (the rep is over before the cue).
fields.fault.cooldown: Milliseconds before the same cue may be repeated. A cue not yet said in this set is always offered before one that has, so this is what paces a cue that keeps being true, not what decides which fault is heard. Good: 7000–9000. Bad: 500 (the coach nags).
fields.fault.unsure: What a fault has to clear when the pose model is not sure of the landmarks it reads — on a side-on move that is the far arm or leg, which the body hides and the model guesses at. vis: every landmark the fault reads must be at least this confident (0–1) for the fault to be judged normally; on a side-on body the near limb sits near 1.0 and the far one around 0.5. Below vis the reading still counts, but only as a large violation: it must pass the threshold by margin, in the reading’s own units (degrees, or percent of the reference length), and hold for persist times as long. floor: below this the landmarks are guesses and the fault does not fire at all. Good: vis 0.75, floor 0.55, margin 12 — on a side-on bridge that leaves the near leg judged exactly as before and drops the far leg from seventeen firings to one. Bad: vis at 1.0 (nothing is ever sure enough), floor at 0 (the far leg is coached on invented positions), or a margin so big the fault can never clear it.
fields.fault.maxCues: How many times one cue may be spoken in a single set. perSet is the cap every fault gets; a rule name overrides it for that rule ("Slow it down" only lands the first time you hear it, so fast is capped at 1), and a move overrides both with "maxCues" on the fault itself. Once a cue has had its say it is not repeated, however true it stays — mid-set is not the moment to keep making the point. The end-of-set summary always names a fault that was capped, so it is said once more when there is time to act on it. Good: 2. Bad: 0 (the cue never fires — remove the fault instead) or 10 (the coach nags all set).
fields.fault.noise: What a fault has to clear on top of its threshold, because the reading is not still even when the person is. Between reps the body has stopped, so every measurement is sampled there and the middle 80% of what it did, halved, is that reading’s own wobble in its own units; a fault must beat its threshold by clear times that — once, even for a fault measured as a change from the start of the rep: the start is read from a body that has stopped, so it does not carry a whole wobble of its own. One pause is whatever that half-second happened to do, so the figure used is the middle one of the last few, which also stops it growing when the feet genuinely move between reps. move / settle: resting is not the same as still (the rep’s descent passes through it), so the clock restarts whenever the reading moves further than move — a share of the rep’s range — and sampling starts settle ms after it stops. still / pauses / min: how much of one pause is sampled (ms), how many pauses are remembered, and how many samples a pause needs to count. Rep moves only: a hold has no still moment that is not the exercise. A hip angle off shoulder, hip and knee wobbles a fraction of a degree and is judged exactly as before; heel-to-toe height, two landmarks a few pixels apart near the floor, wobbles a couple of percent of the shin with the feet flat on the mat, and a threshold inside that fires every rep on nothing. The end-of-set review carries the figure per fault, so the Studio can say when a threshold is too small to be measured. Good: 1. Bad: 0 (a noisy measurement invents faults) or 3 (a real fault has to be enormous to be seen).
fields.skeleton: How the skeleton drawn over the camera is shaped. head: "face" (the nose-and-ears triangle the pose model gives), "ball" (a filled circle and a neck), "circle" (the same outlined, so the video shows through), "dot" (one dot and a neck), "none" (a neck stub only). Good: ball or circle — a head-sized head is what makes the figure read as a person. Bad: face over video, where the triangle looks like a crack in the picture. show: how sure (0–1) the pose model has to be of a joint before it is drawn at all, with a little hysteresis so a limb on the edge does not flicker; dim: sure enough to draw at full strength, fainter below. The arm and leg on the far side of a side-on body sit below these most of the time and stay off the picture instead of flailing. Good: show 0.5, dim 0.7. Bad: show under 0.35, where the model’s guesses about hidden joints get drawn.
fields.camera: How much a phone off its ideal spot is forgiven. level: auto (motion sensor when the phone has one, else the body at calibration), sensor, body or off — turns the picture so gravity is straight down before anything is measured. maxRoll: a bigger roll than this is not corrected (the phone is probably on its side on purpose). tolerance: degrees the person may turn away from the ideal view mid-set before the coach says to turn back; a move can set its own in camera.tolerance. yawPersist: ms that has to hold before it is said. widthRatio: shoulder width as a share of torso length, used to guess the turn when depth is missing (0.55 is typical). unforeshorten: measured (stretch the picture back out only when the turn was read from depth), always, or off. Good: tolerance 20–30. Bad: level off on phones propped on the floor.
fields.fault.severityWeight: How much each severity (1, 2, 3) costs in the score and how it ranks against other cues when two fire at once.
fields.targets: The rep counts and hold seconds a move offers when it does not name its own: choices (what the bubble cycles through) and default. Good: 4–6 sensible steps. Bad: 30 choices.
fields.landmarks: Body points (MediaPipe indices) that must be in frame before a set can start. always = shoulders and hips (11, 12, 23, 24). legs = knees and ankles, added unless the move says upperBody: true.
fields.cannotSee: The sentence shown under 'what the camera cannot see' when a move does not write its own.
fields.standardFaults: The faults added automatically to a tracked move that lists no live fault of its own: shallow (did not reach the target) and fast (rep quicker than minMs) for rep moves, shortHold (came down before the hold was up) for a rep move with repHold, drift (left the held position) for holds. Words only — the numbers come from the move.
fields.side: The Left / Right / Both choice every one-sided move offers: its label, the default, and the wording of each choice. follow: when the limb that is actually moving is not the one chosen, the coach switches to it rather than asking the person to start again — margin is how much further (in the progress reading's own units) the other limb must travel, frames how many frames in a row it must do so. Good: 14 / 12 (about half a second). Bad: a small margin (it flips mid-rep on noise).
fields.weight: The hand-weight choices every move that offers a weight cycles through: 'none', the fixed kilogram steps, and 'custom', which opens a box for the person to type their own. unit is the word shown after the number. Good: 3–4 steps. Bad: ten steps (the bubble becomes a chore).
fields.band: The resistance-band colour scale: the order the bubble cycles through, the name shown for each colour, and the swatch colour drawn. 'none' means bodyweight.
fields.score: How the end-of-set score is built out of 100. faultCost × severity weight per occurrence, capped at faultCap × weight per fault; partialCost per half rep; noRepCap is the most a set with zero reps can score. Holds start at holdFloor and climb with the share of time spent in position; shortHoldPenalty is lost if the hold ends early. tips = how many things-to-fix the written summary carries. speakWeight / speakMax = which suggestions are read out at the end of a set: every fault at least this severity weight, heaviest first, up to this many (and always at least the heaviest one, so a set with only light faults still gets a word). Good: 2 and 4. Bad: speakMax 10 (a paragraph nobody listens to). headlines are read top down: the first row whose atLeast the score reaches is shown.

cannotSee: Anything that only moves toward or away from the phone.

shallow.label: Not reaching the target
shallow.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

fast.label: Too fast
fast.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

shortHold.label: Not held at the top
shortHold.tip: Pause at the top for the full count before coming back down — the hold is the work.

drift.label: Drifting out of position
drift.tip: The hold only counts while you are in the position — ease back in and keep breathing.
